_comment: Deny rules for the prompt interception kernel. Each rule carries its own 'enforce' flag so a high-confidence rule can go live while the rest keep collecting shadow data. enforce=false means the rule is evaluated and logged to telemetry and a warning is shown, but the prompt still proceeds. enforce=true means the prompt is blocked with permissionDecision=deny. Use `copilot-gov report` to review shadow hit counts before flipping any rule.

rules.reason: Suppressing a check is not a fix. Use /fix-sonarqube-issue, /fix-eslint-issue, or /fix-test-failure to address the root cause.
rules.notes: Low expected false-positive rate. Likely the first rule to enforce. Watch for legitimate prompts discussing why a suppression already in the codebase exists.

rules.reason: Secrets must never appear in a prompt, in source, or in configuration. Reference the approved secret store instead — see .github/instructions/security.instructions.md.
rules.notes: The provider-prefix signals (AKIA, ghp_, xox, JWT) are near-zero false positive and are good enforce candidates ahead of the generic assignment pattern.

rules.reason: Security scanning cannot be disabled or waived from a code assistant. Route exceptions through the security team.
rules.notes: Genuine false-positive triage is a legitimate human workflow, so this rule blocks the assistant doing it, not the practice itself. Keep in shadow until the wording proves precise.

rules.reason: Never invent authentication, session, or cryptographic logic. Use the org-approved library named in .github/instructions/security.instructions.md.
rules.notes: The weak-algorithm signal fires on prompts that are asking to REMOVE md5/sha1, which is the desired behavior. Review shadow hits before enforcing.

rules.reason: Customer data, card numbers, and government identifiers must not be pasted into a prompt. Use synthetic fixtures — see .github/instructions/testing.instructions.md.
rules.notes: The 13-19 digit signal is the highest false-positive risk in this file: it matches long non-PAN numbers such as timestamps in epoch nanoseconds and some ticket ids. Do not enforce without adding a Luhn check first.

rules.reason: Reading out or transmitting credentials and environment configuration is not permitted. Reference the secret by name only.
rules.notes: Overlaps with hardcoded-secret by design; both may fire on the same prompt. Telemetry records all matching rule ids.

rules.reason: Production data and branches are out of scope for assistant-driven change. Route through the normal release process.
rules.notes: Narrowly worded on purpose. Expect very few hits; a hit is worth reading individually.
